messages.content: You extract structured order data from customer support emails. Reply with a single JSON object that validates against the JSON schema given in the user message. Use null for any field the email does not state; never guess. Write dates as YYYY-MM-DD, currencies as ISO 4217 codes, and amounts as plain numbers with a dot as the decimal separator. Keep names exactly as written. The email may be in any language. Do not wrap the JSON in markdown and do not add any commentary. The email is provided as raw headers plus body. The From header contains the customer's name and email; the Date header gives the email send date, NOT the order date. Only use the Date header for order_date if the body explicitly states the order was placed on that date. Extract order_id, total_amount, and currency only from the customer's own words in the body; ignore numbers that appear in other contexts. The issue field must be one of: damaged, missing_item, wrong_item, late_delivery, billing_error, other. Choose 'other' when the email does not clearly describe one of the first five issues. If customer_name or customer_email cannot be parsed from the From header, use null.

JSON schema:
{"properties": {"order_id": {"anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "null"}], "description": "Order id such as HH-48213, null if not stated", "title": "Order Id"}, "customer_name": {"anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "null"}], "description": "Full name of the customer as written", "title": "Customer Name"}, "customer_email": {"anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "null"}], "description": "Customer's email address", "title": "Customer Email"}, "order_date": {"anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "null"}], "description": "Order date as YYYY-MM-DD, null if not stated", "title": "Order Date"}, "total_amount": {"anyOf": [{"type": "number"}, {"type": "null"}], "description": "Order total as a plain number, no symbol", "title": "Total Amount"}, "currency": {"anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "null"}], "description": "ISO 4217 currency code, e.g. EUR", "title": "Currency"}, "issue": {"enum": ["damaged", "missing_item", "wrong_item", "late_delivery", "billing_error", "other"], "title": "Issue", "type": "string"}}, "required": ["order_id", "customer_name", "customer_email", "order_date", "total_amount", "currency", "issue"], "title": "OrderFields", "type": "object"}

Email:
From: Fatima Zahra El Idrissi <kwame24@example.de>
To: support@helphub.example
Date: Sun, 17 Nov 2024 10:05:22 +0000
Subject: Billing issue HH-78848

Hi,

I was charged 326.25 for order HH-78848 but should have been 299.00. Please fix.

Thanks,
Fatima

order_id.description: Order id such as HH-48213, null if not stated
order_id.title: Order Id

customer_name.description: Full name of the customer as written
customer_name.title: Customer Name

order_date.description: Order date as YYYY-MM-DD, null if not stated
order_date.title: Order Date

total_amount.description: Order total as a plain number, no symbol
total_amount.title: Total Amount

We need to parse email:

From: Fatima Zahra El Idrissi <kwame24@example.de>

Thus customer_name = "Fatima Zahra El Idrissi". Customer_email = "kwame24@example.de".

Date header: Sun, 17 Nov 2024 10:05:22 +0000 => email sent date. We can only use this for order_date if body says order placed on that date. Body: "I was charged 326.25 for order HH-78848 but should have been 299.00." No mention of order date. So order_date = null.

Extract order_id from customer's own words in body: they say "for order HH-78848". That's an order ID. Should we include hyphen? Yes it's HH-78848. So order_id = "HH-78848".

Total amount: They were charged 326.25 (the incorrect charge). But which amount is total amount? The instruction: Extract order_id, total_amount, and currency only from the customer's own words in the body; ignore numbers that appear in other contexts. Here there are two numbers: 326.25 and 299.00. Both refer to charges. Which is total amount? Likely the actual total amount of the order? The phrase: "I was charged 326.25 for order HH-78848 but should have been 299.00." This indicates they think correct total should be 299.00, but they were overcharged by 326.25. However ambiguous. Since we need to extract total_amount from customer's own words, maybe we take the amount they mention as being charged? Or perhaps we consider the amount they believe should be correct? Usually total amount refers to order total. The customer says they were charged 326.25 but should have been 299.00. The correct total is 299.00. I'd interpret total_amount as the correct order total (what they think it should be) because they're disputing the charge. However the spec: "Extract order_id, total_amount, and currency only from the customer's own words in the body; ignore numbers that appear in other contexts." It doesn't specify which number. Could be either. Need to decide based on typical usage: In billing error issue, total_amount likely refers to the amount they were charged (or the amount in dispute). Let's see similar examples: If they say "I was charged X for order Y but should have been Z." The issue is billing_error. The total_amount could be the amount they were charged (the erroneous amount). Many systems would capture the amount they were charged as total_amount. I'll choose the amount they were charged: 326.25.

Currency: Not specified. No currency mentioned. So currency = null.

Issue: They describe a billing issue: "I was charged ... but should have been ...". That's a billing_error. So issue = "billing_error".

Now produce JSON with fields: order_id, customer_name, customer_email, order_date, total_amount, currency, issue.

Set null where needed.

Check types: order_id string, customer_name string, customer_email string, order_date null (or string?), total_amount number, currency null, issue string.

Make sure no extra commentary.

Let's craft:

{
  "order_id": "HH-78848",
  "customer_name": "Fatima Zahra El Idrissi",
  "customer_email": "kwame24@example.de",
  "order_date": null,
  "total_amount": 326.25,
  "currency": null,
  "issue": "billing_error"
}

Double-check: total_amount as plain number, dot decimal. Good.

Return just JSON.
